A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same nonparametric modern Hopfield framework. The main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and corresponding material can be matched across reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: Appendix E reports original memory-retrieval, multiple-instance learning, time-series prediction, and computational-efficiency experiments.

after.justification: Appendix G retains the work's original retrieval, learning, forecasting, and efficiency results, including benchmark scores and experimental curves.

M1.justification: Theorem 3.2 changes the reported sparse update from selecting terms of a full-memory softmax in v1 Equation (3.9) to normalizing softmax over the selected support in v2 Equation (3.7). This changes retrieval weights, but remains a localized revision within the retained SVR framework, kernels, masking variants, and layer architectures.

E1.justification: Both retain MNIST/CIFAR10 image retrieval, MNIST multiple-instance learning, Elephant/Fox/Tiger/UCSB classification, forecasting on ETTh1/ETTm1/ECL/WTH/Traffic, and synthetic computational benchmarks. No dataset, task, or tested input scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding tables and plots, including Dense and Sparse Hopfield baselines and the same evaluated model variants. Newly discussed methods by Santos and others are cited without being added to experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: The documented splits, metrics, training budgets, hyperparameter searches, bag sizes, forecasting horizons, and efficiency-benchmark dimensions are retained. Remark G.1 newly discloses single-step retrieval throughout; the PDFs do not establish a change from an earlier experimental procedure.

E4.justification: The noise-robustness, memory-size sensitivity, MIL training-convergence, and computational-scaling studies are retained. Expanded discussion adds explanations without new ablations or analytical experiments. Removing v1's composite overview figure does not remove its constituent analyses.

E5.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same run-count and seed descriptions, averaging practices, and retrieval-plot standard deviations. The existing discrepancy between 50 runs in retrieval prose and 10 runs in its caption persists. No new uncertainty estimation or significance testing appears.

E6.justification: Tables 5 and 6 and all experimental plot images retain identical quantitative results. Qualitative reporting changes: v1 Figure 4 groups Random Masked Hopfield among models robust to increasing bag size, whereas v2 Figure 3 emphasizes its accuracy loss. V2 Figure 2 also newly states that smaller k lowers retrieval success, contradicting the adjacent lower-error description.

T1.justification: The sparse normalization changes in Theorem 3.2 and its derivation. V1 Appendix B.5's comparison of upper bounds is replaced by a softmax-weight argument in v2 Appendix D.5 for Corollary 4.1.1. Most formal statements and the convergence and capacity proofs remain unchanged after renumbering; this is a localized theoretical revision.

C1.justification: Both claim a nonparametric Hopfield framework, efficient sparse variants, retrieval and robustness guarantees, exponential capacity, and connections to attention variants. The abstract's shift from 'construction' to 'interpretation' does not materially change these retained contributions.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands applicability and mechanism discussion. Appendix B newly explains difficulties posed by correlated real-world patterns for well-separation assumptions, while consolidating existing convergence and support-inclusion caveats. Remark F.1 distinguishes fixed memory models from trainable layers, and Appendix G adds explanations involving distractor suppression and training dynamics. V1 offered much less interpretation of these boundaries and mechanisms.

D1.justification: Appendix G newly specifies RTX 2080 Ti/Xeon 4214 hardware, PyTorch 1.8.0, RayTune, and single-step retrieval. The code link and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged. However, v1's 20% retrieval-success threshold disappears with its overview caption, and v2 retains the conflicting PyTorch 1.11.0 statement in G.5.

R1.justification: V2 materially revises positioning by explicitly crediting Nguyen et al. with attention's SVR formulation and distinguishing the proposed model from Santos et al.'s Fenchel-Young/SparseMAP approach. It also replaces the Chen et al. kernel attribution with established exponential-kernel references and discusses additional related memory models. These changes address the framework's intellectual relationship to closely overlapping work.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: SVR background moves from Section 2.1 into an expanded Appendix C, limitations become Appendix B, related work becomes a numbered subsection, and references precede the supplement. Experimental narratives and several captions are extensively expanded, alongside broader language and terminology edits.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes a two-column conference main text with a reformatted supplement. Figure 1 is redrawn with explicit theoretical-guarantee boxes. V1's composite Figure 2 is removed while its experimental plots remain separately, and figures, tables, spacing, and captions are extensively rearranged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves attribution, applicability discussion, and implementation disclosure. However, the revised sparse normalization is not propagated consistently: Appendix D.4 retains the full-memory softmax, while new Equation (D.9) incorrectly expresses softmax using unexponentiated inner products. V2 also loses the retrieval-success threshold and introduces contradictory sparsity and software-version descriptions. With unchanged numerical evidence, the clearer exposition and these substantive consistency problems do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
